A thinktank linked to Reform UK has called for the abolition of the state pension and £75bn worth of sweeping tax cuts in a "radical" report likely to influence the party's platform for the next election. The Centre for a Better Britain's report – which also calls for weaker rules for UK banks and Trump-style investment accounts offering £1,000 to newborns – will be formally launched at a private event with City executives on Wednesday. –

Motorists buying a secondhand car with a lot of miles on the clock are likely to find an electric vehicle ultimately more reliable than a petrol vehicle, according to a study. An analysis of 47.4m MOT tests found that after cars were driven 90,000 to 120,000 miles, EVs were about 25% less likely to fail than petrol models of the same age (based on a failure rate of 16.5% versus 22.1%). Beyond 120,000 miles, 16% of EVs failed, compared with 23.5% of petrol cars. The study found relatively little difference between the two fuel types at lower mileages. –

Major indices put in a mixed showing on Tuesday, with the tech‑heavy Nasdaq closing at a fresh record, while the Dow slipped and the S&P 500 ended broadly unchanged.
At the close, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.36% at 51,863.69, while the S&P 500 was flat at 7,764.64 and the Nasdaq Composite saw out the session 0.45% firmer at 27,244.28.
